project.name: Spequlator
project.purpose: A code–documentation consistency analysis and explanation system with a shared analysis engine, developer CLI, and interactive frontend.

product_decisions.decision: Spequlator is a complete academic minor project, not an MVP-only deliverable.
product_decisions.rationale: The deliverable must include a usable frontend, CLI, shared analysis engine, evaluation, tests, and documentation.

product_decisions.decision: The product analyzes code and associated documentation and explains potential inconsistencies or documentation drift using visible evidence.
product_decisions.rationale: This fits the project objective and the available versioned code/docstring data without requiring unsupported five-class labels.

product_decisions.decision: The system must show evidence and uncertainty and may return inconclusive.
product_decisions.rationale: Similarity and diff patterns do not prove runtime behavior or correctness.

product_decisions.decision: CoDocBench is the primary dataset for experiments.
product_decisions.rationale: It contains 4,573 versioned code/docstring records and an official project-disjoint split.

product_decisions.decision: SAFA is supplementary traceability data and remains separate from the primary dataset.
product_decisions.rationale: It contains requirement-to-code trace links but no direct verified consistency labels, and represents one project.

product_decisions.decision: SciCoQA is excluded from the main implementation and reserved for possible future research.
product_decisions.rationale: It concerns scientific paper/code discrepancies, includes synthetic data, and has overlap between real and pooled splits.

product_decisions.decision: Do not infer the original five consistency labels from link presence, similarity scores, or change flags.
product_decisions.rationale: These signals do not establish alignment, partial alignment, missing implementation, missing documentation, or contradiction.

product_decisions.decision: Compare a TF-IDF baseline with pretrained transformer embeddings and a lightly fine-tuned transformer encoder (see D-020).
product_decisions.rationale: This provides a defensible classical NLP versus deep learning comparison without training a language model from scratch.

product_decisions.decision: Use a structured, evidence-grounded report generator; fine-tuned text generation is not required.
product_decisions.rationale: The audited datasets do not provide validated explanation targets.

product_decisions.decision: Preserve CoDocBench's official project-disjoint train/test split.
product_decisions.rationale: This reduces project-specific leakage and keeps evaluation reproducible.

product_decisions.decision: Provide both a developer CLI and a web frontend over the same analysis service/core.
product_decisions.rationale: Both interfaces are required project deliverables and must not duplicate analysis logic.

product_decisions.decision: Use a Python core, Typer CLI, FastAPI backend, and React/Vite/TypeScript frontend unless repository constraints require a documented change.
product_decisions.rationale: This keeps NLP and dataset code in Python while providing a distinct, interactive frontend and a developer CLI. Accepted in v1.2: matches the existing uv/Python 3.13 repo; Vite proxy removes CORS work [R20].

product_decisions.decision: The frontend must be minimal but intuitive, supporting manual input and dataset-example inspection with evidence-first results.
product_decisions.rationale: A focused workflow is more useful and feasible than a large dashboard.

product_decisions.decision: The project must include automated tests, documented evaluation, reproducible setup, and a demo workflow.
product_decisions.rationale: A minor project needs evidence of correctness and reproducibility beyond a working screen.

product_decisions.decision: Evaluate with a stale-vs-updated proxy task on CoDocBench: (old docstring | old->new code) is the stale pair, (new docstring | old->new code) is the updated pair. These proxy labels come from dataset construction, are always called 'proxy', and are never presented as drift ground truth.
product_decisions.rationale: CoDocBench contains only commits where code and docstring changed together [R1], so no real-drift labels exist; the old/new contrast mirrors the dataset's own 'closer to matching version' metric [R1]. Near-trivial docstring edits (25.3% of train [F2]) are reported as a separate stratum. Clarifies D-007: no five-class labels are inferred.

product_decisions.decision: Support two modes: change mode (documentation + old_code + new_code; primary) and snapshot mode (documentation + code).
product_decisions.rationale: Encoding code edits beats inspecting current code alone in prior work [R4]; on train, TF-IDF delta-alignment AUC 0.724 vs 0.565 for snapshot similarity [F3, F4].

product_decisions.decision: Findings come from a transparent rule: rules R1 (documented parameter missing from the signature) and R2 (docstring mentions an identifier deleted from the code) plus delta-alignment signals with dead-bands epsilon learned on TRAIN only and frozen in artifacts/thresholds.json.
product_decisions.rationale: R1 fires 15.3% (stale) vs 7.4% (updated) [F5]; R2 27.8% vs 17.7% [F6]; R2 adapts the OVERLAP(C, deleted) baseline (68.0 F1) [R4]. Rules give exact, checkable evidence.

product_decisions.decision: Pretrained deep-learning signal: microsoft/unixcoder-base pinned at revision 5604afdc964f6c53782a6813140ade5216b99006, mean-pooled, L2-normalised, max_seq_length 512 (256 on <8 cores). Never enable trust_remote_code.
product_decisions.rationale: Apache-2.0, no remote code [R7]; best encoder in snapshot mode on the train sample [F7]; jina-embeddings-v2-base-code failed to load with transformers 5.x [F7]; MiniLM truncates at 256 word pieces [R8].

product_decisions.decision: If the encoder cannot load, analysis still completes with TF-IDF and rules; encoder signal is null and an uncertainty is added. CLI flag --no-encoder forces this.
product_decisions.rationale: Keeps the demo robust to model download and hardware issues (PRD risk list).

product_decisions.decision: Fine-tune sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (revision 1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41) on CoDocBench TRAIN triplets (new code, new docstring, old docstring as hard negative) with MultipleNegativesRankingLoss, 1 epoch, batch 8, lr 2e-5, max_seq_length 128, seed 13. Go/no-go at H3 on a project-disjoint dev split inside train; result is reported either way. If it passes the gate (dev delta-AUC ≥ pretrained MiniLM), it is the live encoder in CLI/API (UniXcoder otherwise); all encoders are reported in the evaluation.
product_decisions.rationale: Pretrained encoders trail TF-IDF in delta mode (300-record train sample: UniXcoder AUC 0.641, MiniLM 0.632, TF-IDF 0.733) [F8]. On a project-disjoint dev split inside train, one epoch lifted MiniLM from 0.624 to 0.649 AUC and the TF-IDF+fine-tuned combination reached the best pairwise accuracy (0.778 vs 0.760) in 371 s on 2 CPU cores [F9]. Not a generator; consistent with D-009.

product_decisions.decision: Statistics: pairwise accuracy (ties = 0.5) and pooled ROC-AUC with 95% project-cluster bootstrap CIs (1,000 resamples, seed 2026), paired difference CIs vs TF-IDF; one frozen test run guarded by --confirm-frozen and a frozen-eval git tag.
product_decisions.rationale: Bootstrap is recommended for NLP metric comparisons [R12, R17]; top-5 projects hold 29.4% of train records [F1], so resampling projects avoids overstated precision.

product_decisions.decision: Serve the API on 127.0.0.1 only; frontend calls /api through the Vite dev proxy; no source text or analytics leave the machine.
product_decisions.rationale: Privacy NFR; Vite server.proxy avoids CORS configuration [R20].

product_decisions.decision: Pin CoDocBench at github.com/kunpai/codocbench commit ee0256da15a07dcf265d5313fe51a269aa7268e0 with recorded SHA-256 checksums; attribute under CC BY 4.0.
product_decisions.rationale: Licence CC BY 4.0 per Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.14251623 [R3]; checksums in docs/REFERENCES.md.

product_decisions.decision: Install CPU-only PyTorch via a uv explicit index.
product_decisions.rationale: On Linux, PyPI torch defaults to multi-GB CUDA wheels [R21]; nothing in the plan needs a GPU.

product_decisions.decision: Refine D-017: R1 is suppressed when the function takes **kwargs; R2 counts toward potential_drift only when no delta signal exceeds its dead-band; provisional eps_tfidf=0.01 until `eval calibrate` (H3).
product_decisions.rationale: Train split: R1 fires on 9.3% stale vs 1.6% updated docstrings (6.0x lift, up from 2.1x). Gating R2 cuts updated-doc flags from 24.4% to 20.1% at eps 0.01 while stale flags move 50.8% -> 48.6%. Coverage about 66% (>= 60% target).

product_decisions.decision: Group CoDocBench projects by owner/project (project_key) for split guards, bootstrap clusters and reporting.
product_decisions.rationale: Repo names 'Python' and 'manim' appear in both splits under different owners (TheAlgorithms vs Yonv1943; 3b1b vs ManimCommunity). Keyed by owner/project, overlap is zero. ManimCommunity/manim is a fork of 3b1b/manim: noted as a threat to validity.

product_decisions.decision: Main evaluation and live app use MiniLM (pretrained and, per D-020, fine-tuned) as the deep-learning signal. UniXcoder (D-018) becomes optional: run only on a GPU or if time remains, reported as an extra row.
product_decisions.rationale: Measured on the build machine (8 CPU cores): MiniLM train cache 283 s; UniXcoder projected about 25-45 min per split on CPU, repeated for test, and the first attempt ended in a machine crash. Train-sample delta AUC was similar (UniXcoder 0.641 vs MiniLM 0.632, F8).

product_decisions.decision: Replace the D-017 'all delta signals must agree' rule with one combined score: the mean of each available delta signal divided by its train standard deviation, with a single dead-band eps calibrated on train (coverage >= 60%). If no eps reaches 60% coverage, calibration picks the most decisive eps and warns.
product_decisions.rationale: With MiniLM, the agreement rule could not reach 60% coverage on train; the old fallback then chose eps with coverage 0.402, about 60% inconclusive. Averaging standardised TF-IDF and encoder signals gave the best pairwise accuracy in feasibility (F9: 0.778 vs 0.760 TF-IDF alone), and lets the encoder contribute to every decision instead of acting as a veto.

product_decisions.decision: Score the RQ4 manual review (60 reports) with an LLM plus a second re-check pass, instead of a human annotator.
product_decisions.rationale: No annotator time left before the deadline. Reported everywhere as LLM-scored, not human-verified; no agreement figure (single scorer).

in_scope: Developer CLI for analyzing supplied code/documentation and dataset examples
Manual input mode for documentation and code
Dataset example mode for CoDocBench records
Unit tests and API/CLI integration tests
Project-disjoint dataset evaluation and manual review
Setup, architecture, dataset, and user documentation
Change mode (old/new code) and snapshot mode
Explainable rules R1 (parameter mismatch) and R2 (deleted-identifier mention)
Light contrastive fine-tuning of a small encoder on CoDocBench train (D-020)
Stale-vs-updated proxy evaluation with project-cluster bootstrap CIs
out_of_scope: Training a language model from scratch
Combining all three datasets into one training corpus
Claiming semantic similarity proves code correctness
Production-scale deployment, authentication, multi-user collaboration, or cloud hosting unless required later
Presenting proxy-task results as real-drift detection rates

codocbench.collection_rule: code and docstring changed in the same commit [R1]

architecture.core: Python package containing preprocessing, comparison, report generation, and dataset adapters
architecture.cli: Typer CLI calling the same core functions as the API
architecture.api: FastAPI adapter exposing validated analysis endpoints
architecture.frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript frontend calling the FastAPI API through the Vite /api proxy
architecture.shared_logic_rule: Business logic belongs in the Python core; CLI and API must not implement separate copies.

change_control.rule: Any change to scope, primary dataset, split policy, model comparison, architecture, or evaluation claims must be recorded as a new decision entry before implementation.

evidence_register: docs/REFERENCES.md (R* = external sources, F* = train-only feasibility runs)
